title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: It much affected me to hear of your afflictions, and the more soto think that it is so difficult for me to come to see you. I have very often thought of you and have had some hopes time back of hearing of your getting better. I may inform you a little of the circumstance of our family.

My dear husband has not missed one fit of the ague yet and has it at this time, a nd our poor sick lad is alive yet but I believe there are but few that see him that thinks he will live long. For hardly i think he has set up ten minutes at the time this three weeks. We are afraid to leave him alone many minutes at the time, for fear he should drop off and we not know of it. And I may say with thankfulness that the rest of our family is about as well at present as is common for us to be. I think I have had my health rather better than common.

closer.salute: So I conclude and remain your affectionate mother,

postscript.label: PS
postscript.p: Please to remember my love to brother & sister Thornton & Jamie. Please to write & let us know how they anyhow are, and how little Edmund is with that wheezing in his throat. And how you all are are. Joseph, it will be matter of joy to me that thee is restored to thy usual health again. My husband join with love to you all
